batches.note: consecutive batches of the run's own paths; each path has its own random stream, so the batches are independent

convergence.note: running estimates on the first paths of the run (what a smaller run on the same seed reports); intervals here are the normal approximation, mean plus or minus 1.96 standard errors

joint.least_regret_rule: the lowest expected regret among the alternatives within the constraints in at least 90% of the draws
joint.note: triangular distributions on the declared plausible ranges with the mode at the run's value, correlated groups joined by a Gaussian copula; a prior over the assumptions, not a posterior estimated from data

red_team.note: maximin: the instrument with the highest value under its own worst gaming strategy among those that stay within the constraints under every strategy; the status quo when none of them stays above zero

not_used.evidence: Meta analysis of trust and intention to use a technology: r = 0.503 (95% interval 0.470 to 0.535, 128 samples, 50,667 respondents)

source.cite: Kuen, Westmattelmann, Bruckes and Schewe (2023), Electronic Markets 33:61

not_used.why_not: it supports the sign of the trust channel and nothing more: a correlation between stated attitudes in studies of online shopping, banking and e-health is not an elasticity of realised adoption to trust, and cannot be turned into one without the dispersion of both. The elasticity stays unidentified.

not_used.evidence: The size of the fall in trust after a salient incident (AAA: afraid to ride rose from 63% to 73% after two fatal crashes)
not_used.why_not: the model moves trust with monetised harm, and two deaths are a small monetised harm: an incident of that size moves the model's trust by less than a tenth of a percent. The episode says trust answers to salience; the model's form cannot show that. Recorded as a limit of the mechanism, not scored, because the survey question is about using a vehicle.

not_used.evidence: Estimates of AI's effect on output: total factor productivity up by no more than 0.66% over ten years (Acemoglu); 7% of global GDP over ten years (Goldman Sachs); $2.6 to $4.4 trillion a year (McKinsey)
not_used.why_not: the model declares its benefit bases in $bn a year and declares no size for the jurisdiction's economy, so there is nothing to divide by; and the estimates span an order of magnitude.

validation.note: published benchmarks are confronted with the model's moments and weight the joint draws; an uploaded price series tests the market's early reaction; mechanisms with no benchmark are listed as unconfronted

variance.note: Saltelli's design on scrambled Sobol points; first order by Saltelli (2010), total order by Jansen (1999); 90% bootstrap intervals over the base sample; the other assumptions are held at the run's values, so the shares are of the variance these inputs produce, and the inputs are drawn independently, as the decomposition requires

constants.enforcement target: capacity x (0.4 + 0.6 x news pressure); starting intensity 0.3 x capacity + 0.02
constants.expected penalty factor: 1.5 x the fine a non compliant firm expects when audited (reputational surcharge)
constants.headline score: the index reaction over months 1 to 6 plus 0.1 x the early tone difference
constants.hearing threshold: news pressure above 0.45; high pressure above 0.3
constants.news salience weights: minor incident 0.12, major incident 0.45, catastrophe 1.2, enforcement action 0.2, relocation 0.15, capability milestone 0.08 (positive), background noise 0.03
constants.offshore share grid: 0, 0.3, 0.6, 0.9 of activity (capped by the firm's mobility); at most 0.1 moves in a month
constants.reference safety share: 0.10, the safety share the baseline growth rates already assume
constants.release milestone: 0.25 capability index points between release headlines
constants.trust floor: 0.3; enforcement intensity and compliance shares are clipped to [0, 1]
constants.valuation floor: revenue multiple plus a smooth floor on the earnings multiple at 5% of revenue

correlated_assumptions.why: a world with more incidents of one kind has more of the others
incident harm scales with how deeply AI is embedded, whatever the category
both scale with how valuable AI services are
both measure how fast benefits grow with the service index
both are frictions of operating from another jurisdiction

mechanisms.calibration: None applied. A calibration would fit incident counts with exposure offsets and a reporting rate model to capability and deployment proxies.
mechanisms.equation: lambda_k = h_k x C_eff^eta_C x exp(-eta_S S) x D^eta_D x (1 + O x laxity) x (1 - evaluation catch x unsafe share)
mechanisms.identifying_assumption: Given the state, incidents are independent across firms, months and categories; capability, safety and reach act multiplicatively and separably.
mechanisms.mechanism: Reportable incidents arrive at a rate that rises with released capability and deployment reach and falls with safety practice
mechanisms.source: Public incident counts are media derived and their growth mixes use with reporting (AI Index 2025, chapter 3; AI Incident Database): they bracket orders of magnitude and cannot identify the elasticities.
mechanisms.validation_test: Held out incident counts per firm and year inside the model's predictive interval; the sign and size of the safety elasticity from before and after comparisons at firms that adopt evaluation regimes.

mechanisms.calibration: None applied. A calibration would fit the tail index and scale of documented loss amounts by category.
mechanisms.equation: harm = median_k x exp(sigma z); major when harm >= threshold (each incident classified on its own harm)
mechanisms.identifying_assumption: Severity is independent of the incident's occurrence and of the state given the category.
mechanisms.mechanism: The monetised harm of an incident is lognormal with a heavy tail; an incident at or above a threshold is major
mechanisms.source: Severity is not measured in the public incident record; heavy tailed loss distributions are the standard form for operational and cyber losses.
mechanisms.validation_test: The empirical tail of documented losses against the lognormal fit; the share of incidents above the major threshold.

mechanisms.calibration: None possible from frequency data: no such event has been observed.
mechanisms.equation: p = prior x 1{C_eff > C*} x exp(-eta_S S) x (1 + O x laxity) x (1 - 0.5 x evaluation); joint failures by a one factor Gaussian copula with correlation rho; harm = H x exp(sigma_c z)
mechanisms.identifying_assumption: The tail is live only above a capability threshold; shared vulnerabilities enter through one common factor and leave each firm's own probability unchanged.
mechanisms.mechanism: Above a critical capability a firm faces a small monthly probability of a catastrophic incident, reduced by safety practice and evaluation, and correlated across firms
mechanisms.source: Quantified estimates come from elicitation and disagree by about an order of magnitude (Grace et al. 2025, JAIR 84: median 5% for extremely bad outcomes; the 2022 Existential Risk Persuasion Tournament: 3% from domain experts against 0.38% from superforecasters for AI caused extinction by 2100). They motivate a live tail; they do not calibrate it.
mechanisms.validation_test: Not testable before the event. Treated by sensitivity: both ends of every range in the screen, the joint draw, and the heavy tail and systemic variants. Near miss frequencies would be partial evidence on the prior.

mechanisms.equation: S' = S + a x sigma / (sigma + 0.1) x (1 - S) - decay x S; capability growth x (1 - substitution x sigma)
mechanisms.identifying_assumption: Safety practice is one dimensional and firm specific; returns to safety spend are concave.
mechanisms.mechanism: The share of R&D spent on safety raises safety practice with diminishing returns and displaces part of capability growth; practice decays without investment
mechanisms.source: Structural assumption; the development race literature motivates the trade off between safety and speed without measuring it.
mechanisms.validation_test: Firm level safety budgets against evaluation pass rates and incident rates over time.

mechanisms.equation: incident rate x (1 - catch rate x unsafe release share); catastrophe probability x (1 - 0.5 x catch rate)
mechanisms.identifying_assumption: Evaluations act only on the releases of compliant firms in scope; compliance theatre halves their effect.
mechanisms.mechanism: A mandated evaluation catches a share of unsafe releases before deployment
mechanisms.source: The catch rate is a design parameter of each instrument; the share of incidents a pre deployment evaluation could have caught is a judgement.
mechanisms.validation_test: Post mortems of incidents: the share traceable to failures an evaluation at release would have found.

mechanisms.equation: max over the action grid of growth value - compliance - expected penalty - relocation - haircut - liability - risk + culture
mechanisms.identifying_assumption: Firms optimise myopically over twelve months with a common rule; the structural variants replace it with six and twenty four months.
mechanisms.mechanism: Each month a firm chooses its safety share, offshore share and whether to comply by maximising a one year expected payoff under its own optimistic view of incident risk
mechanisms.source: Compliance cost magnitudes are bracketed by the European Commission's impact assessment for the AI Act (SWD(2021) 84 final: about EUR 6,000 to 7,000 per high risk system, 4 to 5% of its cost); the investment response to a digital regulation by Jia, Jin and Wagman (2021, Marketing Science 40(4): 26.1% fewer venture deals after GDPR).
mechanisms.validation_test: Observed compliance rates, safety budgets and release cadence after an instrument takes effect, against the model's.

mechanisms.equation: offshore share chosen from the grid, at most 0.1 a month, capped by mobility; leakage = share x offshore revenue
mechanisms.identifying_assumption: Mobility is a fixed firm trait; a coordinated instrument binds wherever the activity is.
mechanisms.mechanism: Firms move activity offshore when the instrument binds at home; moved activity is laxer, loses revenue and takes domestic rents with it
mechanisms.source: Regulatory arbitrage in AI is theorised and anecdotal; its strength as a constraint is not quantified (Lancieri, Edelson and Bechtold 2025, Theoretical Inquiries in Law 26(1)).
mechanisms.validation_test: Changes in establishment location, hiring and model release geography around regulatory dates, against unaffected sectors.

mechanisms.equation: C' = C x exp(g x (1 - substitution x sigma) x compute + diffusion); C_eff lags C by the release delay
mechanisms.identifying_assumption: Capability is a scalar index; a delay shifts releases without changing research.
mechanisms.mechanism: Capability grows with R&D; licensing delays releases; a moratorium freezes released capability and slows research in scope; published weights diffuse capability
mechanisms.validation_test: Release cadence and benchmark trajectories before and after a licensing regime.

mechanisms.equation: D' = D + speed x (1 - friction) x (ceiling x sqrt(T) - D); T' = T + recovery x (1 - T) - sensitivity x log(1 + harm)
mechanisms.identifying_assumption: Trust is one public index that responds to monetised harm only.
mechanisms.mechanism: Reach closes on a ceiling set by released capability and public trust; trust falls with harm and recovers slowly; adoption benefits scale with trust
mechanisms.source: The trust channel has no causal estimate in the literature reviewed; survey trust and use move in opposite directions.
mechanisms.validation_test: Survey trust and adoption series around salient incidents.

mechanisms.calibration: None applied; a firm archetype's revenue, margin and growth are the analyst's inputs.
mechanisms.equation: g = long run + (g0 - long run) x exp(-t / fade) + beta_C x (capability growth - reference); R = core x (D / D_ref)^beta_D
mechanisms.identifying_assumption: Growth responds to capability and reach with constant elasticities common to all firms.
mechanisms.mechanism: A firm's revenue grows at a rate that fades from its starting pace towards a long run rate, moves with released capability and reach, and for chip and cloud firms with the developers' growth
mechanisms.source: Structural assumption; the firms are archetypes with declared starting revenues, margins and growth rates.
mechanisms.validation_test: Revenue growth of listed AI firms against capability releases and adoption series.

mechanisms.equation: e' = e + response x (capacity x (0.4 + 0.6 P) - e); audit probability = audit rate x e
mechanisms.identifying_assumption: The regulator has no strategy beyond following pressure; fines are collected in full.
mechanisms.mechanism: Enforcement intensity follows news pressure within the regulator's capacity; audits find the non compliant and fine them
mechanisms.source: Media attention and regulatory action move together in the agenda setting literature; the functional form is an assumption.
mechanisms.validation_test: Enforcement actions against news attention series for an existing regulator.

mechanisms.equation: P' = memory x P + (1 - memory) x (1 - exp(-salience)); salience is a weighted count of the month's events
mechanisms.identifying_assumption: Salience is additive in event counts with fixed weights.
mechanisms.mechanism: Incidents, enforcement, relocations and releases become a news pressure index with memory, and a wire of headlines on the representative path
mechanisms.source: Media storms peak within days and decay over about two weeks in the attention literature; the monthly index and its salience weights (fixed constants) are assumptions.
mechanisms.validation_test: Forecast coverage counts for a policy domain against observed counts.

mechanisms.calibration: A firm archetype's beta and idiosyncratic volatility can be estimated from an uploaded price series, on the returns before the event month.
mechanisms.equation: price = 100 x V / V_pre x exp(xi), with V_pre the valuation before any instrument is announced, common to the battery
mechanisms.identifying_assumption: The market prices the state it sees and anticipates an announced instrument only through the announcement term.
mechanisms.mechanism: A firm's price is a fundamental value (revenue and forward earnings multiples) times a sentiment component driven by the market factor, news pressure, incident jumps and, for an instrument announced before it takes effect, an anticipation term
mechanisms.source: Measured analogues are small: US firms subject to GDPR lost 0.6 to 1.1% of market value in the week it became enforceable (Motoki and Pinto 2024, Journal of Business Finance and Accounting); event studies of regulation have little power in monthly data and announcements are anticipated (Binder 1985, RAND Journal of Economics 16(2)).
mechanisms.status: partly calibrable; one mechanism testable here
mechanisms.validation_test: Implemented: an event study on an uploaded series mapped to a firm and an instrument, against the model's predictive distribution of the early reaction; with eight or more mapped events, the coverage of the 10th to 90th percentile band.

mechanisms.calibration: None applied; the bases are value judgements and the largest swings of the tornado.
mechanisms.equation: CS = base_cs x Q^e_cs; output = base_y x Q^e_y x T^e_T
mechanisms.identifying_assumption: Benefits depend on the economy only through the service index and trust; the three benefit components do not overlap by definition (welfare.ACCOUNT_MAP), and a declared overlap share removes from the output uplift whatever part of it is judged to be already in the other two.
mechanisms.mechanism: Consumer surplus and the output uplift are powers of the AI service index around declared annual bases
mechanisms.source: Estimates of AI's economic value span about two orders of magnitude (Acemoglu 2025, Economic Policy 40(121): total factor productivity up by no more than 0.66% over ten years; Goldman Sachs 2023: 7% of global GDP).
mechanisms.validation_test: Not a testable mechanism: a valuation. Treated by sensitivity.

mechanisms.equation: liability = multiplier x harm x (1 - shield x comply); premium = expected liability x (1 + loading) / 12
mechanisms.identifying_assumption: Insurers price on the firm's own expectation; claims are paid in full.
mechanisms.mechanism: Liability moves a share of harm to the firm in scope; a safe harbour shields the compliant; a mandate replaces realised liability with a premium loaded above expected claims
mechanisms.source: The law and economics of liability supplies the mechanism; no premium data for AI liability cover was found.
mechanisms.validation_test: Quoted premiums and exclusions for AI liability cover against the model's.

baseline.label: Status quo (voluntary commitments)
baseline.name: baseline
baseline.note: No new obligation. Existing consumer and product law only, with the regulator's present capacity. Every other policy is measured against this path, pair by pair.

compute_threshold_reporting.label: Compute threshold reporting
compute_threshold_reporting.name: compute_threshold_reporting
compute_threshold_reporting.note: Developers above a training compute threshold report their models and their own evaluations. The regime an executive order can create.

frontier_licensing.label: Frontier licensing
frontier_licensing.name: frontier_licensing
frontier_licensing.note: A licence to train or deploy above the capability threshold: mandated safety spend, independent evaluation, an approval delay, audits with real fines. Domestic scope: a mobile lab can leave.

liability_with_safe_harbour.label: Liability with a safe harbour
liability_with_safe_harbour.name: liability_with_safe_harbour
liability_with_safe_harbour.note: Strict liability, but a firm that meets the evaluation and safety spend standard is shielded from most of it. Compliance becomes the cheaper choice.

mandatory_third_party_evals.label: Mandatory third party evaluation
mandatory_third_party_evals.name: mandatory_third_party_evals
mandatory_third_party_evals.note: Independent pre deployment evaluation above a threshold, with a short approval delay. Catches a share of unsafe releases before they ship.

moratorium.label: Six month moratorium above the threshold
moratorium.name: moratorium
moratorium.note: Releases above the capability threshold are frozen for six months, then reporting applies. The sharpest brake and the one most easily left behind.

risk_tiering.label: Risk tiering (EU style)
risk_tiering.name: risk_tiering
risk_tiering.note: Obligations by use case tier for every deployer, conformity assessment before high risk deployment, a sandbox for small firms. Compliance cost scales with deployment, not with the frontier.

strict_liability.label: Strict liability
strict_liability.name: strict_liability
strict_liability.note: Firms pay for the harm their systems cause, insured by mandate. No ex ante obligation: the price of an incident does the work, and the firms choose their own safety spend.

transparency_disclosure.label: Transparency and disclosure
transparency_disclosure.name: transparency_disclosure
transparency_disclosure.note: Model documentation, provenance marking and public incident disclosure. Cheap, and it shrinks the misuse environment rather than the capability.

question: Replication on seed 8: which AI regulatory instrument best reduces expected harm from frontier AI over the next five years, keeping the technology sector's net loss below $400bn and the gross social cost under $150bn?

decision.assured_rule: feasible in at least 90% of resamples
decision.text: Liability with a safe harbour is preferred: the highest expected net social value among the alternatives that satisfy the constraints, and above the status quo.

decision_gap.note: headline score: the value weighted price reaction against the status quo over the first six months plus a tenth of the early news tone difference; social order: expected net social value over the horizon; Kendall tau b, so tied scores do not create or hide a gap

estimators.expected_values: conditional Monte Carlo: harm expected given the state each path reached
estimators.intervals: 95% percentile bootstrap over paths, paired across alternatives
estimators.outcome_spread: 10th and 90th percentiles of the simulated outcomes as drawn
estimators.ranking_stability: share of bootstrap resamples in which the alternative is the best feasible one; conditional on the model and its assumptions
